narrative: Your application was denied because the model estimated a 94% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a very high statistical estimate, so the decision reflects a strong concern about bar-exam readiness rather than a judgment about your potential as a law student. The three most influential factors in that estimate were your third-year class standing, your LSAT score, and your first-year class standing, in that order. Each pushed the prediction toward failure. Your third-year class-rank decile was 2, compared with an average of about 5.8 among accepted students, which was the strongest warning signal. Your LSAT score of 28 was also below the accepted-student average of about 37 and added substantially to the concern. Your first-year class-rank decile of 2, compared with an average of about 6, reinforced the same pattern. Together, these academic indicators suggested a higher risk of bar-exam difficulty. This prediction is not a final judgment of your ability. You should request a human review of your file, speak with an admissions advisor about whether updated grades or a stronger LSAT score could be considered, invest in structured LSAT preparation, and consider additional academic work or legal experience before reapplying.
